demand.reason: Global celestite strontium mineral consumption is estimated at roughly 500,000 metric tons annually, placing it within the high-demand band of 100,000–1,000,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is projected to remain flat to stagnant. Following the legacy collapse of CRT television glass, its core modern applications in ferrite ceramic magnets, drilling fluids, and pyrotechnics are stable but lack growth drivers, placing it in the flatlining/stagnation band.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Iran produced about 250,000 of the 450,000 tons of celestite mined in 2025 (56%), ahead of Spain (22%) and China (18%), placing mining diversity in the 50–65% band (Score 3).


Refining: Downstream strontium carbonate processing is concentrated across China and Germany, with the single largest producer commanding between 50–65% of global output (Score 3).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global strontium resources exceed 1 billion tons. At current consumption rates of a few hundred thousand tons, known economic reserves represent hundreds of years of supply, which is effectively limitless (>100 years).


Diversification: USGS lists reserves only for China (12 million tons) and Iran (2 million tons) and calls world reserves large, so an HHI cannot be computed; the score is kept at 2 as a judgement.

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): strontium nitrate is the irreplaceable chemical input for military pyrotechnics, signal flares, and tracer rounds requiring high brilliance. Healthcare & Biomedical (+0.5): used in strontium ranelate for osteoporosis and strontium-89 for bone cancer radiotherapy. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): utilized as celestite in drilling fluids and heavy pigments.


Sector presence scores total 2.5 across 3 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +1.0, yielding an objective composite score of 3.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Barium ferrite substitutes in low-cost permanent magnets with moderate high-temperature performance penalties. Barite replaces celestite in standard drilling fluids, matching the criteria where substitutes are commercially deployed with manageable trade-offs (Score 2).


Recyclability: Strontium is consumed entirely in highly dissipative configurations like incinerated pyrotechnics, dissipated drilling fluids, and low-concentration mixed scrap. No secondary supply chain exists, matching the effectively zero recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Strontium mining involves straightforward open-pit celestite extraction followed by basic soda ash roasting to produce strontium carbonate. The processing technology is highly mature, universally documented, and moderately complex.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline features no notable pipeline developments. Due to the flatlining and mature nature of global demand, there is a complete absence of capital deployment or new primary projects, scoring the maximum pipeline constraint.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India mines no celestite, so its ore is imported (Score 5). Strontium carbonate itself is made in India: Vishnu Chemicals has close to 10,000 tonnes of capacity, about half of it in use in mid-2026, selling mainly to flexible-magnet makers.


Strategic Posture: Strontium is officially listed on India's critical minerals framework with customs duties exempted. However, lacking a dedicated KABIL mandate or foreign equity investments, its posture aligns with early-stage declared strategic intent (Score 3).

price_volatility.reason: The unit value of celestite imports fell from $210/t (2021) to $82/t (2023) and was $160/t in 2025 (USGS), a swing of more than 100% in a thin market (Score 4).

capability.name: Strontium
capability.next_move: Win customer approvals and fill the new carbonate plant, lock in celestite supply, then move into ferrite magnets.
capability.what_india_has: Vishnu Chemicals, the first maker of strontium carbonate in India: a plant at Visakhapatnam with about 10,000 t/yr of operating capacity, expandable to 17,000, commercialised in 2025. Celestite ore is imported, now free of customs duty.
capability.cost: About Rs 110 crore in all: the Rs 52 crore acquisition in 2024 plus later capital spending.

stages.world: Celestite: Iran 250,000 t, Spain 100,000 t, China 80,000 t of 450,000 t (2025).
Celestite is converted to strontium carbonate; processing is concentrated in China and Germany.
stages.india: Vishnu Chemicals, Visakhapatnam: about 10,000 t/yr, running at 20 to 25% in early 2026, against Indian demand of about 4,000 t/yr.
Regular sales, mainly to magnet makers, were expected from early FY27 once customers approved the product.

stages.world: Ferrite magnets, pyrotechnics, drilling fluids, aluminium casting.
stages.india: Demand of about 4,000 t/yr, until now imported, mostly from Mexico and Belgium.
